name: Michigan Island Light
notes: R1 has the characteristic as unknown; fixed white is the assumption. The 1869 tower (the 1929 skeleton tower isn't built yet). 'The unwanted lighthouse'.

name: La Pointe Light
notes: R1 lists the 1858 Long Island light as active but with the lens and the site unknown; it may have been retired when the 1897 Chequamegon Point light was built. Placed on Long Island's harbor shore as a small fixed white light until the sources say more. Fog signal: a bell, one stroke every 15 s, assumed for the harbor approach.

name: Raspberry Island Light
notes: Lit 1863. West channel near Bayfield: a weak beam, but the keeper reports fast. Fog signal: a hand-rung bell, two strokes every 20 s. Assumed for the busy west channel: R1 doesn't record the station's fog signal yet.

name: Outer Island Light
notes: Lit 1874. The most remote light, on a tall tower. Fog signal: a steam whistle, one 5 s blast every 30 s. Assumed: R1 doesn't record the station's fog signal or its code yet.

name: Sand Island Light
notes: Lit 1881, fixed white until 1921. Brownstone dwelling; guards the Sevona shoal.

name: Devils Island Light
notes: The tower stands but the 3rd-order lens doesn't arrive until June 1901, so in 1900 it shows a temporary fixed red light: a known gap in coverage on the exposed north edge. The tower's build (a steel skeleton) is ⚠️ from memory, to check against NPS photos.

name: Chequamegon Point Light
notes: Lit 1896-97 on the tip of Long Island, eroding. R1 has the lens and the characteristic as unknown; fixed white is the assumption.

name: Duluth South Pier Light
notes: R1/R1a: the canal's south pier light is a temporary tower in 1900 while the pier is rebuilt in concrete (1898-1901); the permanent tower comes in August 1901. Stands on the outer end of the game's south canal pier. The characteristic is unrecorded: fixed red is an assumption that sets it apart from Superior Entry. The canal had a steam fog signal; its 1900 rhythm is assumed.

name: Superior Entry Pierhead Light
notes: R1a has the 1900 setup at Superior Entry as unknown; one source has a pierhead light built in 1885 when the Minnesota Point light was retired. Placed on the outer end of the south (Wisconsin Point) pier, where the later breakwater light stands, as a small fixed white light. The bell is assumed.

name: Minnesota Point Light
notes: Lit 1858 at the Superior Entry end of Minnesota Point; extinguished in 1885 per most sources (one says 1913). Standing dark in 1900: the brick tower without its lamp, an abandoned lighthouse and hideout candidate (R1a).

name: Two Harbors Light
notes: First lit April 1892 on Lighthouse Point, the east side of the Agate Bay entrance: a red-brick light station with a square tower on the keeper's house and a 4th-order Fresnel lens (R1). The 1892 characteristic is unverified; fixed red is assumed. The station had a steam fog signal; its 1900 rhythm is assumed.
